title: Question 5.2
statement_text: Is is true that for every positive integer $\mu$ there exists a polynomial $\mathsf{p}_{\mu}$ such that every $K_{t,t}$-free graph $G$ with $\operatorname{tree\textnormal{-}\mu}(G)\leqslant\mu$ satisfies $\operatorname{tree\textnormal{-}\alpha}(G)\leqslant\mathsf{p}_{\mu}(t)$?
context_text: $H$-free means having no induced subgraph isomorphic to $H$; in particular $K_{t,t}$-free excludes the biclique $K_{t,t}$ as an induced subgraph. For a tree decomposition $\mathcal{T}$ of $G$, its independence number is the maximum of $\alpha(G[B])$ over its bags $B$, and its induced matching number is the maximum size of an induced matching $M$ of $G$ such that some bag contains at least one endpoint of every edge of $M$. The tree-independence number $\operatorname{tree\textnormal{-}\alpha}(G)$ and the induced matching treewidth $\operatorname{tree\textnormal{-}\mu}(G)$ (introduced by Yolov) are the minimum of these measures over all tree decompositions of $G$. Always $\operatorname{tree\textnormal{-}\mu}(G)\le\operatorname{tree\textnormal{-}\alpha}(G)$, but complete bipartite graphs have induced matching treewidth $1$ and unbounded tree-independence number. Abrishami et al. proved that every $K_{t,t}$-free graph with $\operatorname{tree\textnormal{-}\mu}(G)\le\mu$ has tree-independence number bounded by a function of $\mu$ and $t$ (exponential in $\mu$ even for fixed $t$); the authors improve this to $\operatorname{tree\textnormal{-}\alpha}(G)=O_t(\mu^{3t^2+1})$, polynomial in $\mu$ for fixed $t$. A bound polynomial in both $\mu$ and $t$ is impossible: for every $t$ there is a graph that is $K_{t,t}$-free and $tK_2$-free (so of induced matching treewidth less than $t$) with tree-independence number $2^{\Omega(t)}$. This does not rule out a bound polynomial in $t$ for each fixed $\mu$, which is what the question asks.
paper_title: Induced matching treewidth and tree-independence number, revisited

title: Question 5.3
statement_text: Is it true that for classes of graphs with bounded induced matching treewidth, tree-independence number is bounded from above by a polynomial function of the induced biclique number?
context_text: $H$-free means having no induced subgraph isomorphic to $H$; in particular $K_{t,t}$-free excludes the biclique $K_{t,t}$ as an induced subgraph. For a tree decomposition $\mathcal{T}$ of $G$, its independence number is the maximum of $\alpha(G[B])$ over its bags $B$, and its induced matching number is the maximum size of an induced matching $M$ of $G$ such that some bag contains at least one endpoint of every edge of $M$. The tree-independence number $\operatorname{tree\textnormal{-}\alpha}(G)$ and the induced matching treewidth $\operatorname{tree\textnormal{-}\mu}(G)$ (introduced by Yolov) are the minimum of these measures over all tree decompositions of $G$. Always $\operatorname{tree\textnormal{-}\mu}(G)\le\operatorname{tree\textnormal{-}\alpha}(G)$, but complete bipartite graphs have induced matching treewidth $1$ and unbounded tree-independence number. Abrishami et al. proved that every $K_{t,t}$-free graph with $\operatorname{tree\textnormal{-}\mu}(G)\le\mu$ has tree-independence number bounded by a function of $\mu$ and $t$ (exponential in $\mu$ even for fixed $t$); the authors improve this to $\operatorname{tree\textnormal{-}\alpha}(G)=O_t(\mu^{3t^2+1})$, polynomial in $\mu$ for fixed $t$. A bound polynomial in both $\mu$ and $t$ is impossible: for every $t$ there is a graph that is $K_{t,t}$-free and $tK_2$-free (so of induced matching treewidth less than $t$) with tree-independence number $2^{\Omega(t)}$. The induced biclique number of $G$ is the largest nonnegative integer $t$ such that $G$ contains an induced subgraph isomorphic to $K_{t,t}$; it is a lower bound on tree-independence number (up to a constant) and has been studied in several recent contexts. The authors note that this question is an equivalent restatement of asking whether, for every $\mu$, there is a polynomial $p_\mu$ such that every $K_{t,t}$-free graph $G$ with $\operatorname{tree\textnormal{-}\mu}(G)\le\mu$ satisfies $\operatorname{tree\textnormal{-}\alpha}(G)\le p_\mu(t)$.
notes: Explicitly stated by the authors to be equivalent to Question 5.2.
paper_title: Induced matching treewidth and tree-independence number, revisited

title: Question 5.4
statement_text: Is is true that for every positive integer $\mu$ there exists a polynomial $\mathsf{p}_{\mu}$ such that every graph $G$ with $\operatorname{tree\textnormal{-}\mu}(G)\leqslant\mu$ and clique number at most $\omega$ satisfies $\chi(G)\leqslant\mathsf{p}_{\mu}(\omega)$?
context_text: Abrishami et al. proved that any class of graphs with bounded induced matching treewidth is $\chi$-bounded, i.e., the chromatic number can be upper-bounded in terms of the clique number. However, the bound obtained is at least exponential in the clique number, and the authors ask whether a polynomial bound suffices — i.e., whether such graph classes are polynomially $\chi$-bounded.
paper_title: Induced matching treewidth and tree-independence number, revisited
